title.narrative: Amu Bukhara Irrigation System Rehabilitation Project

description.narrative: The proposed project is located in Bukhara Province and two districts in Navoi Province in the central part of Uzbekistan. The project will ensuer a sustainable and reliable water supply for irrigated agriculture in the main command area of 250,000 ha in the Amu Bukhara Irrigation System (ABIS) and drinking water for 725,000 population.

Output: 3. The capacity of BISA, ISAs, WCAs, and farmers to adapt to climate change increased. This will also support the government strategy to diversify crops and ensure food security in the project area. Indicator: Women make up an average of 20% of WCA secretariats in selected OFISs by 2022, compared with 0% in 2012. Achievement: 3.7 Progress/Status: The indicator c initially set a target to comprise women an average of 20% of the secretariats of Water Consumer Associations (WCAs) in the project area by 2022. This target emerged from a baseline socio-economic survey, which highlighted that women exhibit effective skills in managing household resources, including water usage. Women were recognized for their careful and rational approaches to planning, consumption, and resource management, which made their participation valuable in promoting fair water distribution within WCA farmer communities. The target also aimed to enhance gender participation within the water sector. WCAs as a non-governmental organization with elected secretariats, were previously offering opportunities to increase women's involvement, support equitable water planning, and promote sustainable water management practices.
However, in 2022, structural reforms in Uzbekistan transferred the functions of WCAs to different non-government entities based on land ownership conditions, affecting the implementation of this target. Furthermore, on January 5, 2024, Presidential Resolution No. PP-5, On Measures to Improve the Water Resources Management System and Increase Efficiency at the Lower Levels, established a new 'Water Delivery Service' responsible for managing water resources at the farm level.
This restructuring transferred on-farm water planning and management to the government, rendering the original DMF target inapplicable. Data Source: BISA, M&E, and PMU reports
